chunks: He said: 'O my people! Is my clan more honored to you than Allah, whom you have taken as a back turned to you? Surely my Lord is encompassing of what you do.'
ai.seo_question: What does Hud (AS) mean when he says his people made God 'behind their backs'?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Hud, Prophet Hud (peace be upon him) confronts his people's tribal arrogance, questioning if their lineage is more precious to them than the Creator. The phrase 'behind your backs' (khala'akum) signifies their casual neglect of divine accountability, while the attribute 'Al-Muhit' (The All-Encompassing) serves as a reminder in Shia exegesis that God's knowledge surrounds all hidden and apparent deeds. This highlights the transition from tribal loyalty to individual responsibility before the Divine.
